name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
summary: A seated cable vertical pulling exercise performed with a wide overhand grip to build the latissimus dorsi and upper back.

aliases.text: Jalón al pecho con agarre ancho

setup: Adjust the machine's thigh pad so your legs are firmly wedged underneath with feet flat on the floor.
Stand up to grip the long bar with a pronated (overhand) grip slightly wider than shoulder width, usually just outside the bar's bends.
Sit down, anchoring your thighs snugly under the pads, and allow your arms to extend fully overhead with a slight backward lean of five to ten degrees.
steps: Initiate the movement by drawing your shoulder blades down and back.
Pull the bar down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down toward your back pockets.
Touch or bring the bar close to your clavicle while keeping your chest lifted and spine neutral.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then slowly extend your arms under control back to the fully stretched starting position.
instructions.breathing: Inhale before initiating the pull, exhale as you draw the bar to your chest, and inhale as you return the bar overhead.
cues: Drive your elbows to your back pockets.
Control the stretch at the top.

common_faults.fault: Excessive torso swing and leaning back to heave the weight down.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a stable torso with only a slight natural backward lean, using the lats rather than momentum.

common_faults.fault: Pulling the bar behind the neck.
common_faults.correction: Always pull the bar down in front of your face toward your upper sternum to protect the cervical spine and shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the range of motion short at the top.
common_faults.correction: Allow your arms to fully extend and your scapulae to upwardly rotate for a full stretch on the lats each rep.

precautions: Ensure the thigh support is locked securely to keep you anchored to the seat during heavy sets.
